content.title: About
content.content: Canned cooked beets with added fat is a ready‑to‑eat product made by boiling beets, then sealing them in jars with a small amount of vegetable oil. The product retains the sweet flavor and bright red color of beets, while the added fat enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beets are rich in beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A during cooking.
Canning allows storage for 2‑3 years without major loss of nutrients.
A modest amount of added oil increases the bioavailability of lutein and beta‑carotene.
Beets have been cultivated for over 5,000 years, making them one of the oldest vegetables.
The red color comes from betanin, a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: High in antioxidants
items.content: Betanin and lutein protect cells from oxidative stress and support eye health.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Nitrate compounds in beets help dilate blood vessels and maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Improves vitamin absorption
items.content: Added fat assists the body in absorbing fat‑soluble vitamins A and K present in beets.

items.title: Supports liver detoxification
items.content: Betaines and glucosinolates help eliminate toxins and support liver function.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may react to the oil used in the product.

items.title: Betanin may color bodily fluids
items.content: Large amounts of beets can temporarily turn urine or stool pink; this is harmless.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Beets have a moderate acidity that may cause discomfort for those with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat straight from the jar: add it to salads, soups, stews, use as a side dish for meat or fish, or simply enjoy as a snack. It can also be gently warmed in the microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days, sealing the lid tightly.

content.title: About
content.content: The Chicken Fillet Wrap Sandwich, grilled, is a fast‑food item featuring tender grilled chicken fillet wrapped in a soft wheat tortilla together with vegetables and sauce. It is a convenient, protein‑rich meal popular in chain restaurants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sandwich is often sold as part of a combo with fries and a drink.
The chicken fillet is usually marinated in spices and lemon juice before grilling, giving it a fragrant flavor.
The wrap format allows the sandwich to be eaten without utensils.
In some regions the recipe includes fresh lettuce, tomato and a yogurt‑based sauce for a lighter taste.
Grilling retains more protein and reduces added fat compared with deep‑frying.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Grilled chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Grilling reduces added fat, making the sandwich a more diet‑friendly option.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones and immune health.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Added lettuce, tomato and cucumber increase dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and seasonings can be high in salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although lower in fat than fried options, the sandwich still provides calories from the tortilla and sauce.

items.title: Cooking safety
items.content: Undercooked fillet may harbor pathogens; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to hold in one hand; you may cut it in half for a smaller bite. Add extra sauce or fresh veggies if desired to boost flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best consumed immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in a microwave or on a grill before serving to restore a slight crisp.

ice-cream-soda-flavors-other-than-chocol.title: Ice Cream Soda, flavors other than chocolate

content.title: About
content.content: Ice cream soda is a carbonated dessert drink that blends a creamy ice‑cream flavor with a light fizz. It is offered in a variety of flavors, excluding chocolate, such as vanilla, strawberry, mint, caramel, and other fruit‑based options.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recipe for carbonated ice cream appeared in the early 20th century in the United States.
Ice cream soda is often served in glass cups with a straw to preserve the bubbles.
In some countries it is called “fizzy ice cream” or “sparkling ice cream.”
Non‑chocolate flavors are especially popular with children because they are less sweet and more vibrant.
The carbonation is created by adding food‑grade sodium bicarbonate and an acid (e.g., citric acid) that react when the drink is poured.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Certain flavors (e.g., vanilla) contain riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The carbonated water component helps maintain fluid balance, especially on hot days.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Sugar and lactose supply rapid glucose, useful for a quick energy boost.

items.title: Mood uplift
items.content: Sweet taste and gentle fizz can stimulate serotonin release, improving mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Carbonated drinks can cause heartburn or bloating in some individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey requires avoiding the product.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of the creamy base and sugar, a serving can be calorie‑rich; moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve ice cream soda chilled, typically in a glass with a straw. You can garnish with fresh berries, mint leaves, or a sprinkle of cinnamon to enhance flavor. Avoid vigorous stirring, which can dissipate the carbonation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, consume within 24 hours to retain fizz. Discard if ice crystals form or the taste changes.

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp cocktail is a classic appetizer consisting of boiled or sautéed shrimp served in a glass with a sauce made from mayonnaise, ketchup, and spices. It is often garnished with lettuce, lemon wedges, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The shrimp cocktail originated in the United States in the early 1920s and quickly became a party staple.
The traditional cocktail sauce contains tomato ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice, and Worcestershire sauce.
Shrimps used are usually small (15–30 g each) and peeled, leaving the tail for easy handling.
The dish is commonly served in tall glasses or cups to emphasize its “cocktail” character.
Variations may include avocado, mango, cucumber, or hot sauce for a bolder flavor.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Shrimp provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of shrimp contain about 99 kcal, making the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Mineral rich
items.content: Shrimp are high in selenium, zinc, and iodine, important for thyroid function and immunity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B12 and B6 help maintain nervous system health and metabolism.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Shrimp can accumulate heavy metals and microplastics; choose reputable suppliers.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Traditional sauce can be high in salt; reduce salt or make the sauce at home.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cocktail chilled in a glass, arranging shrimp around a bed of lettuce. Offer the sauce on the side or drizzle it over the shrimp. Add a lemon wedge and fresh dill or parsley if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked shrimp in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. The sauce is best made fresh, but can be kept refrigerated for up to 3 days.

tea-iced-instant-black-decaffeinated-pre.title: Iced Instant Black Decaf Tea Sweetened with Low-Calorie Sweetener

content.title: About
content.content: This is a caffeine‑free instant black tea designed for cold preparation. The dry powder dissolves quickly in cold water, creating a refreshing drink with a sweet taste provided by the low‑calorie sweetener (5250).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea is the world’s second most consumed beverage after water.
Decaffeination preserves most flavor compounds while removing caffeine.
Instant tea was invented in the early 20th century and became popular for its convenience.
Low‑calorie sweeteners allow a sweet taste with reduced energy content.
Iced instant tea is often used in sports drinks and cocktails.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Black tea contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Caffeine‑free
items.content: The lack of caffeine makes it suitable for people sensitive to stimulants.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: A cold beverage helps maintain fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Sweetener 5250 provides sweetness without significantly increasing calories.

items.title: May aid digestion
items.content: Tannins in black tea can help normalize digestive processes.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tea components.

items.title: Sweetener sensitivity
items.content: Although low‑calorie, the sweetener may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people.

items.title: Tannin content
items.content: High tannin intake can reduce iron absorption when consumed in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dissolve one serving (about 2 g) in 200 ml of cold water, stir or shake well. Drink it as is, or use it as a base for cocktails, smoothies, or fruit punches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sachets or jar of powder in a dry, cool place away from moisture and direct sunlight. After opening, keep the package tightly sealed to prevent moisture absorption.

tuna-noodle-casserole-with-mushroom-sauc.title: Tuna Noodle Casserole with Mushroom Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Tuna noodle casserole with mushroom sauce is a hearty dish that combines pasta, canned tuna, mushrooms, and a creamy sauce. Baked until golden, it offers a comforting, protein‑rich meal that has been popular in American home cooking since the mid‑20th century.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in post‑war America as an inexpensive way to use canned tuna.
Mushroom sauce is often made from sautéed mushrooms, flour, and milk, making it lighter than traditional cheese sauces.
Tuna provides a high amount of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.
The casserole stores well in the fridge and can be reheated, making it a common make‑ahead family meal.
Variations may include peas, broccoli, or cheddar cheese for extra flavor and texture.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Tuna supplies EPA and DHA, which support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A serving delivers about 20‑25 g of protein, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna and mushrooms are good sources of niacin, B12, and riboflavin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from sauce
items.content: The creamy mushroom sauce adds calcium, contributing to bone health.

items.title: Fiber from pasta
items.content: Using whole‑grain pasta boosts dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Tuna can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna is often salty; choose low‑sodium varieties when possible.

items.title: Calorie‑dense sauce
items.content: The creamy sauce adds calories and saturated fat; consider using reduced‑fat milk or cutting back on the amount.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage can allow bacterial growth; keep the casserole refrigerated and consume within 3‑4 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the casserole hot, often alongside a green salad or steamed vegetables. Sprinkle grated cheese on top a few minutes before the end of baking for a golden crust. Leftovers reheat well in the microwave or oven.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the casserole to room temperature, then place it in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
